observation.visible_scene: A close-up, shallow-focus shot of a lit sparkler held upright in the right-center of the frame against a blurred background: a dark vertical post in the middle, a windowed area with a bright circular bokeh highlight on the left, and a pale wall/door with a horizontal seam on the right. The sparkler's tip burns as a small white-hot point with a reddish coiled wire just above it and a long thin stick extending downward.
visible_changes: The sparkler burns continuously throughout; the white-hot glow point stays near the same vertical position while the blackened, consumed coil above it lengthens from a short stub in early frames to a taller squiggly black line in later frames.

Bright sparks are emitted radially from the glow point, with the direction, length and density of the spark trails changing from frame to frame (e.g., long horizontal trails to the right in some frames, downward and leftward trails in others).
Thin wisps of smoke appear and grow more prominent over the excerpt, drifting upward and to the left of the burning tip, clearly visible in the later frames.

The background layout (bokeh circle, dark post, horizontal lines) and the sparkler's overall position in the frame remain essentially fixed, indicating the sparkler is held steady rather than translated; only minor handheld-level variation is evident.
outside_clip_unknowns: When the sparkler was lit and when it will burn out (the clip is a temporal crop, with the burning already ongoing at the first frame and still ongoing at the last).
Whether a person is holding the sparkler (no hand or support is visible).
The exact material of the wire/coating and the true nature of the blurred background surfaces.
uncertain_details: Any small camera drift or handheld jitter is hard to separate from the sparkler's own slight movement given the blurred background.
The precise vertical migration of the active burn point is subtle and partly inferred from the growing black residue above it.
